leverage.exposure: No leverage exists and none can open. Every recommended action, taken together with both live bids, still leaves the balance comfortably positive, so the zero-score-on-negative-balance rule is not in play. The lock is nearly four days out, which is the one piece of slack in this position.

binding_gap: The squad is a body short of legal, and the shape is the reason it is awkward rather than simple. Kickbase caps defenders at five, and with only two midfielders the sole legal shape is 5-2-3, which needs three attackers. That has one useful consequence: a single defender landing is enough to fix the penalty outright, because five defenders, two midfielders and three attackers is exactly a legal eleven. Both live bids are defenders, so either one landing closes the gap. Only if BOTH auctions fail does the penalty stand, and that is the whole job of the Krattenmacher body.

verdict.headline: Two reversals this run, both forced by the same event: the Nguefack auction was lost overnight to PhiL95 at a record clearing premium.
verdict.headline_short: Two reversals this run, both forced by the same event: the Nguefack au
verdict.detail: Two reversals this run, both forced by the same event: the Nguefack auction was lost overnight to PhiL95 at a record clearing premium. That kills the plan the last run left behind, because its named fallback body was Skov - and Skov turns out to be injured with no minutes at all this season. So the cheap-body leg is rebuilt from scratch, and the record premium itself changes how the live bids should be priced. Nothing here opens a negative position, and nothing here is a sale.

sell.reason: No sale is possible this run and none should be attempted - the squad is below the floor for it. The sale ladder, once a sale becomes legal, has been corrected in an important way: at twelve players the one available sale must be a DEFENDER, because selling the spare defender leaves a legal shape while selling Sylla leaves one that fills nothing at all. Widmer is the first sale on that basis - he sits outside the eleven either way, so losing him costs nothing in points while stopping a fast bleed on a small asset. Bernardo goes instead of him only if that injury flag is still live near the lock, in which case selling him banks far more, stops a much faster bleed, and removes a probable zero from the eleven. Selling Sylla is a different problem: it needs a third midfielder or fourth attacker first, and the German window shuts this evening. Only one body on the board resolves in time to make that sale legal today.

buy.reason: The top move is to raise the Maluze bid, and it contradicts the last run's explicit instruction not to raise anything. That instruction was correct against the premium band as it stood yesterday and is wrong against the band as measured now: the Nguefack clearing overnight was almost double the previous record, and both record premiums are cheap contested Kickbase listings - exactly what Maluze is. The standing bid looked bold yesterday and now sits in losing territory. He is worth pressing on because his points-per-euro is the best on the board by an order of magnitude, and because the verification is as clean as it gets: a twenty-year-old who started the opener and signed a new contract the same day is not about to be dropped. Hold ter Horst where he is - his bid already sits at the top of the mid-price band, and the record premiums come from sub-three-million listings where a huge percentage is small money; they do not transfer to a player of his price. Behind those two, Krattenmacher is the eleventh-man insurance and deliberately resolves after both auctions, so the decision can be sized against the actual squad count rather than guessed now. Amoako sits behind him as a narrow, conditional alternative and only for one reason - he is the only fit outfield body that resolves before the German deadline this evening, so he is the only route to selling Sylla today. That trade is roughly break-even on expectation: real premium and a small points cost in the fielded eleven, against protecting a speculative departure. It is a judgement call on how much the Brugge story is believed, not an automatic buy. Ljubicic was re-examined and stays avoided: verified fit and a full-match starter, but the price per point is poor and taking him would crowd out the Maluze raise, which is the better euro.

VERIFIED, dated: Ligainsider - FIT, no injury or suspension flag; 24.07.2026 "Krattenmacher zurueck im Teamtraining" after a minor July knock; signed from Bayern 12.06.2026 through 2030. Honest limit: 1 appearance, 0 starts, 32 of 194 minutes, a bench option - he is a body, not a scorer, and he does not enter the best XI. WHY HE IS STILL THE PICK OVER THE OTHER BODIES: cheapest fit outfield player on the board with a POSITIVE ap; Amoako 1.953.327 has ap 0 and 0 starts, Nadir 2.424.073 has ap MINUS 11, Elfadli 2.288.995 is a sixth defender in a squad that already caps out at 5, Skov and Sauer are injured. Bid 2.900.000 = +68,97% over mv: deliberately inside the cheap-listing high cluster now measured at +72,17% (Vogt) and +135,52% (Nguefack), because 1,2M of premium is trivial against a 100-point penalty. CONDITIONAL: only needed if the squad is below 12 after the ter Horst and Maluze auctions resolve, or if the Sylla sale is to be unlocked later in the window. AFFORDABILITY: 9.700.000 + 3.600.000 + 2.900.000 = 16.200.000 against cash 20.527.522, leaving +4.327.522. No leverage.

The Awortwie-Grant clearing is however a genuine premium datapoint worth keeping: +11,43% over mv on a contested Kickbase listing for an injured player, which sits between the manager-ask low cluster and the Ebnoutalib/Campbell high cluster and further supports bidding the HIGH cluster on Kickbase board listings.
